key_insight: MOSAIQC improves quantum circuit cutting by using hybrid warm-start plus refinement optimization to jointly place wire and gate cuts while supporting mixed-size hardware partitions.
engineering_relevance: It offers a more practical way to reduce circuit-cutting overhead for near-term quantum hardware, improving the trade-off between solution quality, runtime, and scalability.
method: Hybrid warm-start optimization followed by refinement
Supports both wire cuts and gate cuts
Uses a fast approximate quadratic assignment solver to place mixed-size hardware partitions
evidence_signal: Compared with the baseline, the paper reports a mean local fidelity improvement of 19.56% ± 6.17%, a 2.88× runtime improvement, and an average 16.84% cut reduction.
watch_item: The method is heuristic and relies on approximate solvers, so performance may depend on circuit structure and partitioning quality rather than guaranteeing optimal cuts.
paper_title: MOSAIQC: Mixed-topology-aware Optimization for Scalable Approximate noise-Informed Quantum circuit Cutting
